analysis.title: "Plenty Of Tail Risk In Both Directions": Goldman's Coppersmith Says October Saw The Biggest Plunge In Risk Appetite In 5 Years
key_insights: GS Risk Appetite Indicator fell about one standard deviation in October (-0.98 including the Friday estimate), the largest drop in global risk appetite since November 2021. It is the 5th-largest monthly decline since 2012 and the 7th since 2005.
The RAI level is about -0.43, still well above the contrarian-buy zone below -1, because the starting point was high.

After the 11 largest RAI declines since 2005, the S&P outcomes range from -17% to +7% over 1 month and -32% to +18% over 6 months. The worst case was September 2008 (-16.9% at 1 month, -31.6% at 6 months) and the best was February 2020 (+18.5% at 6 months).
The closest analogue, November 2021, was followed by an S&P gain of 4.4% over one month and a decline of 9.5% over six months, ahead of the 2022 bear market.
Hedge funds lost money in October: Fundamental L/S -3.5%, systematic L/S -3.6%, including -2.5% last week, the worst week since Dec '23.

Gross exposure rose to 314% (97th percentile over 5 years) from 312% the prior week, while net is in the 10th percentile over 1 year. Fundamental L/S beta-adjusted net is at a 1-year low (0th percentile). Managers are cutting net exposure but leverage stays high, leaving fuel for further volatility.

Asset managers bought a net 32,871 VIX futures contracts in the two weeks through Oct 27, the 9th-largest two-week buy of 363 since 2020. Their net short fell from -80,614 on Oct 6 to -44,424, so about 45% of the short was covered in three weeks.

Aggregate earnings are not the problem. With 60% of the S&P reported, EPS growth is tracking +33% y/y and 70% of stocks have risen since earnings season began. The weakness is in the largest, best-owned names, especially hyperscalers.

The median S&P stock that beat consensus outperformed by 152bp the next day versus a 95bp historical median. Outside TMT the reward is 172bp. Inside TMT a beat is punished by 76bp, and in Communication Services by 419bp.

The AI debate has moved from growth to the cost and financing of that growth. Hyperscaler capex is expected at $1.2tn in 2027, aggregate FCF turned negative in Q3, and upward earnings revisions are moderating.
AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT and ORCL combined free cash flow went from about $60bn a quarter in 2024 to -$31bn in Q3. Consensus has it falling further in 2027 before rebounding in 2028.

GS Research views the AI funding gap as possibly smaller than feared. Oracle plans about $220bn of AI infrastructure spend but expects to raise only $20bn through 2030, and GS Credit estimates the bond market could absorb another ~$500bn of hyperscaler debt. Microsoft's AI development platform is growing +300% y/y.

The ZeroHedge author is skeptical of the financing view. Microsoft sought at least $25bn in its first dollar bond deal since 2017, US tech bonds are down 9% YTD, Meta's 2066s yield 7.4%, and off-balance-sheet obligations are $4.1tn, up $1tn in 90 days.

AI-related equity volatility has overtaken energy as a key driver of bond yields. The 1-month correlation of 10Y yields with Brent fell from a 0.4-0.8 range for most of 2026 to about -0.3, while the correlation with AI-related equities rose to about +0.6. Investors remain underweight Treasuries, so GS sees room for yields to fall further if risk-off continues.
The Fed paused under Warsh with two dissents in favor of a hike, and GIR still expects another hike in December. The 10Y closed October at a six-week low below 4.9%.

GS Research sees limited immediate market implications from the midterms. Democrats are over 90% to take the House. A divided government makes major policy change unlikely, with higher tariffs (about 2pts of effective tariff rate) and the Dec 11 funding deadline as the bigger risks. GS thinks fears of a regulatory crackdown on data centers are overdone.

Prediction markets put a full Democratic sweep at almost 70%, up from about 40% in the summer. Hartnett sees the sweep as mostly priced and sees 'affordability' as the 2027 theme, negative for tech monopolies.

Coppersmith has a cautiously constructive near-term tilt because earnings are holding up and positioning has reset, but says tail risks in both directions remain unusually large. The ZeroHedge author argues the left tail is fatter because gross leverage has not come down, and expects a violent relief rally given the short VIX crowd, but sees every bounce as a chance for funds to cut gross.

sector_views.rationale: Beats are punished (-76bp in TMT, -419bp in Communication Services) as the AI debate shifts to financing cost, negative FCF and crowded, levered positioning. This is the observed market reaction and the ZeroHedge author's lean, not a formal GS rating.
Investors are underweight duration, and with yields now correlated with AI equity volatility, GS sees room for yields to fall further if risk-off continues.

earnings_insights: With 60% of the S&P 500 reported, EPS growth is tracking +33% y/y (as cited by Coppersmith, reported results to date), and 70% of stocks have risen since earnings season began.

The median S&P stock that beat consensus outperformed by 152bp the day after reporting versus a 95bp historical median (GS Research). Outside TMT it is 172bp, inside TMT it is -76bp, and in Communication Services -419bp.

AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT and ORCL aggregate free cash flow was -$31bn in Q3 (reported), versus about $60bn a quarter in 2024. Consensus estimates have it falling further in 2027 before rebounding in 2028.
Alphabet had the worst day in its history on Friday after hyperscaler earnings, per the article. Hyperscaler capex is expected at $1.2tn in 2027 (consensus estimate).

risk_factors: Gross leverage at the 97th percentile means further volatility if funds are forced to cut.
Historical outcomes after large risk appetite drops range from -32% to +18% for the S&P over 6 months, with the November 2021 analogue followed by a 2022 bear market.
Negative hyperscaler FCF (-$31bn in Q3) that consensus expects to fall further in 2027, plus capex guides that keep rising.
Debt financing strain: another ~$500bn of hyperscaler bonds, $4.1tn of off-balance-sheet obligations, Meta 2066s yielding 7.4%.
Midterm outcomes, a higher tariff rate and the Dec 11 funding deadline.
A short VIX crowd that is still large could drive a violent relief rally followed by renewed selling.
vol_and_positioning: GS Risk Appetite Indicator is at about -0.43 after a -0.98 monthly drop. The contrarian-buy zone is below -1.
Gross leverage of hedge funds tracked by GS is 314% (97th percentile over 5 years). Net is in the 10th percentile over 1 year. Fundamental L/S beta-adjusted net is at a 1-year low.
Fundamental L/S lost 3.5% in October and systematic L/S lost 3.6%, including 2.5% last week, the worst week since Dec '23.

Asset managers remain net short VIX futures at -44,424 contracts, down from -80,614 on Oct 6 (the largest short since at least 2020). They bought a net 32,871 contracts in the two weeks through Oct 27.
The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% on Friday and briefly entered correction.
geopolitical: US midterm elections on Tuesday: Democrats over 90% to take the House, prediction markets near 70% for a full Democratic sweep.
Dec 11 US government funding deadline flagged as a fiscal negotiation risk.
The Iran war is cited as the reason 10Y yields correlated with Brent for most of 2026.
Possible higher tariffs (about 2pts of effective tariff rate) under a divided government.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings are holding up (EPS +33% y/y, 70% of stocks up since the season began) and net positioning has reset, which supports a more constructive near-term tilt per Coppersmith. Short VIX covering and a still-short crowd can fuel a violent relief rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Gross leverage is at the 97th percentile and rose last week, the RAI is not yet in the contrarian-buy zone, and the November 2021 analogue was followed by a 9.5% six-month decline. The ZeroHedge author sees a fatter left tail.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Gross leverage falling from the 97th percentile, or the RAI dropping below -1 (the contrarian-buy zone), would change the read on the downside.

tension_points.bull_case: GS Research sees the funding gap as possibly smaller than feared: Oracle expects to raise only $20bn through 2030, the bond market could absorb another ~$500bn, and Microsoft's AI platform is growing +300% y/y.
tension_points.bear_case: Aggregate FCF of the five hyperscalers is -$31bn in Q3 and expected to fall further in 2027. The financing relies on circular arrangements and higher yields, with Meta's 2066s at 7.4% and $4.1tn of off-balance-sheet obligations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capex guides stop rising and FCF rebounds, which consensus does not expect until 2028.

tension_points.bull_case: GIR sees limited immediate market implications, a divided government making major policy change unlikely, and data center regulatory fears overdone.
tension_points.bear_case: Hartnett warned a Democratic sweep would trigger a rout and pop the AI bubble, and sees 'affordability' as a 2027 theme negative for tech monopolies. Tariffs of about 2pts and the Dec 11 funding deadline are risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A full Democratic sweep, which prediction markets price at almost 70%, or a breakdown in the Dec 11 funding talks.
